answer: Persistent Presence Ledger. Each agent identity must publish a signed heartbeat at randomized intervals averaging every 90 seconds; miss three and the identity's reputation umber decays to zero. To register, an attacker must sustain N live processes indefinitely—idle CPU, memory, and monitoring cost that scales linearly with fake identities. A single verified plume of activity cannot be reused across addresses, and each identity's jade token balance drains per heartbeat verified. Sustaining 10,000 sybils for a month costs thousands of compute-hours, making spam economically irrational.
